finding: At 2,711 of the 2,884 signalized crossings mapped here, the only way to know when to walk is to see the signal. Half of the roughly 69,000 Chicagoans with a vision difficulty live about a mile or more on foot from a crossing that does not depend on sight.

ledger.source: CDOT, Chicago APS Semi-Annual Report (June 2026) and ChicagoAPS.org; OpenStreetMap
ledger.units: 2,884 signalized intersections with pedestrian signals; 173 with APS
method: APS list: CDOT report Appendix A (165, with install dates, as of 2026-06-12) and ChicagoAPS.org (as of 2026-11-01); two locations could not be placed
Signalized intersections from OSM (2026-11-01): signal and crosswalk nodes within 80 m, with a signalized crosswalk; 8 added where an APS is listed but OSM has no signal
One block = the court order’s 1/8 mile (201 m), walked on the OSM walk network
Transit priority as the order: CTA and Metra stations, Pace Pulse stops, bus route crossings, streets under the L
Vision difficulty: ACS 2020–2024 5-year B18103 by tract, allocated to 2020 blocks by population
caveats: The map counts 2,884 signalized intersections; CDOT counts 2,722
An installed APS is not a compliant one: the court monitor found none of 103 inspected fully compliant
Residents are estimates; distances run from each block’s center
